title: US reference intakes put adult water at about 2.7 to 3.7 liters a day
summary: The MedlinePlus encyclopedia gives an adult water reference of 91 to 125 fluid ounces, which is 2.7 to 3.7 liters.
body: The MedlinePlus water encyclopedia, reviewed 9 July 2025, says some water comes from foods and some is made during metabolism, and that drinks and liquid foods also supply it. The Dietary Reference Intake it prints for water is between 91 and 125 fluid ounces, or 2.7 to 3.7 liters, per day for adults. If intake is too low, it says body fluids fall out of balance and dehydration follows, and that severe dehydration can be life threatening. The range is an adult reference on that page. It is not a bottle count for an infant. A separate card covers what dehydration feels like in first aid.
